clue.text: (& 21dn.) What drives 10/9 to improve bust with appropriate implant

indicators.note: an implant is something placed inside the body, so one piece is put within the other
bust means broken, so the combined letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: both words taken as written
fit means appropriate or suitable

explanation.surface: Reads like a breast enlargement, with a fitting implant, being what powers tax-haven firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' and 'implant' look like cosmetic surgery, but bust means broken and the implant is FIT added to the letters of 'to improve'. 10/9 is OFFSHORE COMPANIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The desire to make money is the incentive behind business activity, and economists call it by this fixed phrase.

clue.text: see 26dn.
Digger's party about to do a U-turn?

parts.note: the Labour Party, a UK political party

indicators.note: a U-turn sends you back the way you came, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A question about a political party reversing its policy, Private Eye style.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual worker who digs ditches and trenches is the classic example of this kind of worker.

clue.text: Casual insertion in a dry crack

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an insertion is something put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: TT is teetotal, someone who stays dry
a temp is a casual, temporary worker

explanation.surface: A sounds like a builder casually filling a crack in dry plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: TT sits around the casual worker, and A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a crack at something is an informal way of saying you make a go or try at it.

clue.text: Love to slate old Soviet district

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
to slate someone is to criticise them severely, to blast them

explanation.surface: Someone who loves laying into a former Soviet region.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional administrative division in the USSR, and still in Russia and Ukraine, is called by this term.

clue.text: Admit heroin's got into high centre of local politics

indicators.note: getting into something means ending up inside it, so these pieces sit within another word

parts.note: high and tall are synonyms
to own up is to admit
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A confession that heroin has reached the high-ups in local government.
explanation.definitionFit: A council's offices and debating chamber are housed in this civic building, the seat of a borough's administration.

clue.text: Force member on a duck's arse

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
taken as written
DA is the abbreviation for the duck's arse, a 1950s swept-back hairstyle

explanation.surface: A crude image of some member of a force perched on a duck's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The DA was a greased teddy-boy haircut shaped like a duck's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588, is a naval force.

clue.text: Boat put out by Conservative, care of weed

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or upset, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A Tory pushes a boat out while looking after some weed.
explanation.definitionFit: The weed is an old informal name for the smoking leaf, as in giving up the evil weed.

clue.text: see 10ac.
(& 9dn.) "Oh, Cameron, piss off!" — involved with last of the tax avoiders?

indicators.note: being involved means tangled together, so the shouted words are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the outburst, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the

explanation.surface: An angry outburst at David Cameron, whose family was caught up in the 2016 Panama Papers tax-haven row.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron's late father had a fund in Panama, hence the jibe; the E from 'the' completes the seventeen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms registered in low-tax jurisdictions abroad exist largely so owners can legally escape paying domestic levies.

clue.text: Gutless Miliband's bad management

indicators.note: having no guts means the insides are missing, so letters are taken from the middle
something bad has gone wrong, so the remaining letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the Labour leader's name with the central LIB taken out

explanation.surface: A jibe that a spineless Ed Miliband ran things badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led the UK Labour Party until 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin is the informal clipped form of administration, the running and organising of an office or business.

clue.text: Artist who vomits right away

indicators.note: sending something away removes it, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: one who retches, heaving as if to be sick
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An artist who is promptly sick, perhaps at the sight of their own work.
explanation.definitionFit: A printmaker who cuts designs into metal plates with acid is a kind of artist.

clue.text: To be the centre of admiration, grasp Brenda's thing

definitions.text: To be the centre of admiration

parts.note: to grasp is to hold
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, and a royal court is her thing

explanation.surface: Getting hold of something belonging to the Queen to win admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes someone surrounded by an audience of admirers, presiding like a monarch among courtiers.

clue.text: Leader, not fashionable, for instance around Washington, scoffs

indicators.note: the word for fashionable is in, and not means it is removed

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, the Russian leader
in means fashionable

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: say means for instance
WA is the abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: An unfashionable leader, perhaps Putin, gobbling food around Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it greedily, and this phrasal verb also means to consume a lot.

clue.text: Disorder with reckless Clare appropriating House

indicators.note: appropriating means taking for oneself, so one piece is taken inside another
reckless means wild and careless, so the name is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A reckless Clare grabbing a house, perhaps a politician in a property scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: This infectious bacterial disease is an illness, and disorder can mean a sickness of the body.

clue.text: Their age difference is something from the past

indicators.note: a difference is a change, so the letters are altered in their order

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An age gap between a couple described as a relic of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: What is inherited from earlier generations, such as traditions and historic buildings, is handed down from former times.

clue.text: Pissed claret? I object!

indicators.note: pissed is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk claret-drinker protesting, perhaps when accused of being sozzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest, but it is the noun meaning a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are general nouns for a thing or item, as in an article of clothing.

clue.text: Somehow manage to act like frotteurs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: get by, coping without too much trouble
second meaning, read literally: frotteurs get sexual pleasure from pressing against strangers

explanation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb for coping is read literally as rubbing along against people, which is what a frotteur does in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means coexisting or getting by tolerably, while its literal reading describes rubbing against people.

clue.text: Outsize windbag has name for U-turn exponent

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a windbag who talks too much is a bore
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An oversized gasbag is put forward as a champion of the political about-face.
explanation.walkthrough: George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer 2010-16, was mocked for reversing budget measures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor became notorious for abandoning policies, so Private Eye casts him as a master of reversal.

clue.text: Theatrics surrounding Switzerland's old currency

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing on all sides, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: theatrics are dramas
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Talk of Swiss money fuss: theatrics around Switzerland's former currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece used these coins until the euro replaced them in 2002, so they are a former national unit of money.

clue.text: see 1dn.
Showing plenty of front, youth welcomes thus getting married

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: a boy is a youth
so means thus
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A bold young man takes a wife, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Front can mean the chest, and a woman with a large bust shows a lot of it.

clue.text: Police force let off — that's the spirit!

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheer as the police are let off the hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and resilience, as in showing your mettle, is spirit in the sense of pluck.

clue.text: Support cut by Tories' no. 1? Believe!

indicators.note: cutting trims off the end, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a truss is a supporting frame or bandage

indicators.note: number one is the first in line, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Tories

explanation.surface: A slogan of Conservative support cut back, with a cry of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust someone is to have faith in them and accept what they say.

clue.text: Force flattened, having pocketed one grand

indicators.note: pocketing something puts it inside, so those letters go within the other word

parts.note: an oblate spheroid is flattened at the poles
I is the Roman numeral for one
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone forced flat after pocketing a thousand pounds, perhaps a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind someone by duty or compel them to act is the verb's meaning, close to compel.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Certain habits pleased the likes of the Sun

parts.note: glad means pleased
rag is a dismissive name for a newspaper such as the tabloid Sun

explanation.surface: Some habits pleased tabloid newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; 'habits' means clothes, as in a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment, and this informal phrase names one's best clothes for a special occasion.

clue.text: Secure First Lady, Republican's ultimate pay back

parts.note: to secure something is to get it
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the end letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Republican

explanation.surface: Landing a First Lady as the Republican's crowning revenge, in a US election year.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking revenge to settle a score means paying someone back for a wrong.

clue.text: Almost the finish of Cameron? In good time

indicators.note: the finish is the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Cameron
in good time means early

explanation.surface: Wishing David Cameron's downfall were sooner, as it nearly came in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverbs share a sense of not quite, falling just short of completeness.
